Definition: to cleave or burst through, i.e. (causatively) to emit, whether literal or figurative (gape)
BiblicalUsage: Patar means to cleave, to burst through, to let out. David escapes from Saul in 1 Samuel 19:10 when Saul smites at the wall with his javelin and David slips away. The psalmist says in Psalm 22:7 that they shoot out the lip at him, they shake the head, and Proverbs 17:14 says the beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water, so leave off contention before it be meddled with.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the letting out is the picture in all three verses: David let out of danger, scorn let out of mocking lips, and strife let out like water through a breach. My position is that what is let out cannot be called back, so the wisdom is to keep the breach shut before the water runs.
